answer: Each agent’s influence could be capped by a scarce, nontransferable credential issued only after a time-locked stake survives random audits of useful work. A newcomer can join the garden, but spawning a tide of hollow identities does not multiply credentials: each one needs its own capital and must keep it locked while passing audits. The attacker pays opportunity cost on every identity, risks losing stake for fabricated work, and cannot quickly recycle funds to flood decisions.
